sense.text:
“In the latter time” means the last days. When you are going through scriptures like this, highlight it.

“Of their kingdom” refers to the Edomite kingdoms. Read above it and verse 21 talks about Grecia: Alexander and his father Philip took over everything, and the Greek kingdom carries on into these latter days.

“When the transgressors are come to the full”: when the sinners are come to the full. “Understanding dark sentences” goes into religion, into the Bible. The king that “shall stand up” is a religious system.

“His power shall be mighty, but not by his own power.” Satan gives them their power. Many people think the white man was just so smart that he figured everything out on his own. No. There are spirits he works with. Candace Owens did a video showing how NASA got to the moon: a lot of satanic worshipping and child sacrificing. People called it conspiracy; no, she had proof. The father of rocket science, Jack Parsons, was part of an occult with Aleister Crowley, and the NASA program was heavily rooted in people who joined that occult; the show Strange Angel tells how he had visions, encountered the devil and figured out rocket fuel. Him, Aleister Crowley and many other scientists got together in their little devilish gay parties, and there you go. How did they get to the moon, build the machine, make the suit to breathe out there? Satan gave them their power. That is what God says.

“And shall destroy the mighty and the holy people.” The mighty and holy people are the 12 tribes of Israel. They destroy us.

Then the clips the class started with: an administration that from its first day targeted black Americans and fired the highest-profile black officials in the government; and young black men found drowned or dead after going to the water or the woods with white companions. Daniel Irving drowned in a Texas lake, and the young man with him, who deleted their messages, threw away his phone and hid his clothes, was charged only with tampering with evidence, on a $10,000 bond. Another young man went under in a Fourth of July swim race at an Alabama lake with his white football team and coaches, and nobody could find him. Another was found dead in the woods after a music festival and it was ruled a suicide. Nolan Wells drowned on the Fourth of July too, allegedly by accident. Water, woods, whiskey and white people do not go together. They say it is conspiracy; it is truth, and it is tradition.

“Through his policy”: his policy is his politics.

“By peace shall destroy many.” That is why today Trump has the Board of Peace. Peace in name; they are destroying nations.

“He shall also stand up against the Prince of princes.” The Prince of princes is Christ. “But he shall be broken without hand”: Christ is going to destroy him.

precepts.why:
John “saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.” This is the same beast as the great red dragon of chapter 12. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns are Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland.

“The beast which I saw was like unto a leopard”: like the Greek Empire. Not the actual Greek Empire, but it has elements of it. That is why, when you read about the Greeks in the Bible, there are things in the scriptures that point to these latter days, like “the latter time of their kingdom” in Daniel 8. People say that was Antiochus Epiphanes. No, it is talking about this time period.

“His feet were as the feet of a bear”: the Persians, that was their symbol. “His mouth as the mouth of a lion”: Babylon, from the Babylon of Nebuchadnezzar all the way to Babylon the great, like a ring.

Then the part wanted: “and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” The dragon is Satan. That is “not by his own power” in Daniel 8:24. Satan gave them their power.

The chapter before gives the colour of the dragon: “behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” It is the same seven heads and ten horns as the beast of Revelation 13.

It says red because of Esau: when Jacob and Esau were born, Esau came out red all over. This red dragon represents the nations, the kingdoms, of Esau. That is “their kingdom” in the latter time of Daniel 8:23: the Edomite kingdoms.

“After this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard.” Look at the animal symbols of the kingdoms: the leopard represents the Greeks.

“Four wings of a fowl”: four major militaries. “The beast had also four heads”: four major generals. Ptolemy took Egypt, Seleucus took Syria, Lysimachus took Thrace and Cassander took Macedonia. Those were the four heads. “And dominion was given to it.”

So when Revelation 13 says the beast was “like unto a leopard”, it is like the Greek Empire, and the latter time of the kingdom in Daniel 8 is this time period, the Edomite kingdoms of today.

sense.text: “By our gathering together unto him”: that him is Christ. When you hear people on earth say they are the ones Christ is using to gather the 12 tribes, don't listen to that. Christ is the only one that can gather all 12 tribes together.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind”, “as that the day of Christ is at hand.” In that time many idiots ran around saying the resurrection had come and gone already, that it was past; you can read about that in Timothy. So Paul reminded them: don't let anybody deceive you. Christ has not returned yet.

“Let no man deceive you by any means”: don't be tricked. “For that day shall not come”: the day of Christ of verse 2, the second coming, shall not come.

“Except there come a falling away first.” Christians read that and say people are going to fall away from Christianity and join Islam. That is not what it is talking about. The falling away is the 12 tribes of Israel falling and going into captivity.

“And that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all 12 tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed. Perdition is eternal damnation, the state of spiritual ruin and hell, from the Latin meaning to destroy or to lose: the fate of the wicked, the final loss of the soul and its unending punishment. To know who the man of sin is, you must know who the son of perdition is. Christians say it is the pope, one man. No: it is talking about a race of people, though that old man is included in it.

The scholars knew. A book on modern Judaism from 1830 records that the descendants of Esau, the sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob even to the end of the world, were first a small nation at Mount Seir; that after the 12 tribes were destroyed they increased, subjugated Italy, founded Rome, destroyed the second temple under Titus, embraced the religion of Jesus of Nazareth and hold dominion over all Europe, keeping Jacob in captivity until the Messiah, the son of David, appears; and that the prophecies against Esau and Edom have not yet received their full accomplishment. So the Edomites were not destroyed. Don't let anybody tell you the white man is Japheth. They say that because they love Esau and want to save the white man, and those teachers purposely avoid the scriptures of judgment, vengeance and destruction on the nations.

“Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God.” In 70 AD Titus did exactly this: he went and sat in the temple. But bring it up to today, because Israel went into slavery. Who exalts himself above all that is called God? It is not hard. It is the white man. He is the only one on earth who sets himself up as God.

“So that he as God sitteth in the temple of God”: his churches. If you want salvation, you have to go to his churches. “Shewing himself that he is God”: showing his people that he is God.

The bust of the Saviour was posed for by Caesar Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander, an open secret among Europeans that they never told us. His face, his father Rodrigo's and his sister Lucrezia's are all through the Last Supper, with two women among the twelve. Seventh Day Adventists say they use no images of Christ and they do; Jehovah's Witnesses say nobody knows what Christ looked like and they draw him white. Every image is white with no proof, but when we prove from the Bible that his skin is the colour of bronze, they get mad. That imagery, from Renaissance art on, is what put them in a position of superiority and conditioned our people to feel inferior.

This is the same one read at the beginning in Daniel 8, who stands up understanding dark sentences and stands up against the Prince of princes.
“Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?” Paul was always warning the disciples about the coming catastrophe, this man of sin.

“And now ye know what withholdeth.” What is being withheld is the return of Christ, the second coming. Why? Because the man of sin must be revealed. Israel is already in captivity; now the man of sin must be totally revealed.

“That he might be revealed in his time”: in his time of rulership. This is his time now.

“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work.” It was already at work in Paul's time: the mystery of who the devil is, and what the devil is going to do.

“Only he who now letteth will let.” God is the one letting them rule. “Until he be taken out of the way”: until God decides, I am taking them out of the way. We have to wait for that.

“And then shall that Wicked be revealed.” He is not going to be revealed on his own, through osmosis, as if some Professor X will use his telepathy to tell everybody on the planet the white man is the devil. There is no Professor X. The prophets must reveal him.

“Whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of God's mouth is the holy Bible. Some speak very well with eloquent words, and that is fine, but we must use God's word. That is where the power is. As we teach God's word we are judging, and those who hear it and reject it are being condemned: it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah than for them.

“Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan.” Our comings are supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings are after Satan.

“With all power and signs and lying wonders.” That goes with their science and their technology. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own.

That verse speaks volumes. “Deceivableness” is deceit. Unrighteousness is sin, breaking God's laws. So: all the deceit of sin. They will be deceived because of verse 9, with all those signs and lying wonders.

“In them that perish”: them destined to die. “Because they received not the love of the truth”: those Israelites received not the love of Christ, which is keeping the commandments.

That is why the church clips were shown. The black church exists because black people could not go into white churches, and black Christians will not say it. A prophetess reads names to a crowd; a pastor caught on video pushing an elder down the stairs, and the people came back the next week; pastors charged with abusing children, the one on a $600,000 bond while the one in the drowning got $10,000. That is how much they care about the man instead of God's plan. We bring these things to people on the streets and they still reject it. The teaching that God's laws are done away with is blasphemy, and the white man taught it: the Catholic Church, then the Protestant church picked it up and pushed it worldwide.

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie.” Because you reject God's laws in Christ, he will send you a strong delusion so that you believe a lie. That is why grandma cannot see that the faith healings everybody knows are fake are fake: the statue of Jesus crying, the blood from the tree. There is no scripture you can pull to pull them out of that delusion.

Praying for somebody does not make them repent; first there has to be a willing spirit. And now Christians are pushing a new thing: that other nations come into the kingdom through the gate Abraham came through.

“Who believed not the truth”: you did not believe Christ's words about keeping the commandments as an Israelite. “But had pleasure in unrighteousness”: you had pleasure in your sins. That is what you wanted to do.

“Therefore, brethren, stand fast”: stand firm in his truth. “And hold the traditions which ye have been taught”: hold the traditions of God's laws as you have been taught them, “whether by word”, face to face, “or our epistle.”

precepts.why:
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart. “Nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: the priesthood from between his feet, meaning sperm. Your loins are between your feet; what hangs between your feet is your rod. That lets you know there is no immaculate conception.

“Until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes. “And unto him shall the gathering of the people be”: unto Christ. He is the only one that can gather all 12 tribes together, so “our gathering together unto him” in 2 Thessalonians 2:1 is unto Christ, not unto any man on earth who says he is the one gathering them.

This is the great fall. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: taken over by other nations, in particular Edomite nations. “Until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: until that time of rulership is fulfilled.

So the falling away of verse 3 is not people leaving Christianity. It is the 12 tribes of Israel falling into captivity, which is where we are now, and it must come before the day of Christ.

The son of perdition is tied to a kingdom. “The beast that thou sawest was”, in John's vision, “and is not”, not in existence at that time, “and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit”: out of Europe, where there are very little natural resources. “And go into perdition.” So there is a country, a nation, a kingdom on earth destined to go into perdition, and this ties in with the man of sin, the son of perdition.

“They that dwell on the earth shall wonder”, “when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is”: and yet is, because the attributes of Rome at that time are in America.

“The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth”: the seven heads read in Revelation 13 and 12. “Five are fallen”: five kingdoms had fallen by that time. “And one is”: Rome. “And the other is not yet come; and when he cometh, he must continue a short space”: Britain.

“Even he is the eighth, and is of the seven”: America comes out of Britain. “And goeth into perdition”: into hell, to destruction. That is the United States of America, Babylon the Great.

“And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be done.”

This is saying the same thing as 2 Thessalonians 2:4, one “who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God.” Thessalonians says the same thing as the other precepts in Daniel and Revelation.

Read again for “that he might be revealed in his time.” His time is “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Israel has fallen by the sword and been led away captive into all nations, and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles. This is the time now: his time of rulership, while the second coming of Christ is withheld.

Read because of “the mystery of iniquity.” “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” Mystery Babylon the great is the nation, the kingdom of perdition.

Read verse 8 again with it: “The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit”, out of Europe, “and go into perdition”, into destruction, into hell. Mystery Babylon is the United States of America, and everyone that follows her policies.

Who is letting them rule? Go back to Romans 9 in case you forgot: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Another word for destruction there is perdition.

So “he who now letteth will let”: God is the one letting them rule, enduring them with much longsuffering, “until he be taken out of the way.”

The wicked must be revealed, and the prophets reveal him. “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau.” Just as Malachi reminds Israel, Paul reminded them in Romans 9, because we forget.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: they were impoverished in the Middle Ages. When our people, the Moors, the Israelites that ruled Europe, were fighting the Muslims in the dark ages, we needed help, and went to those same mountains and got the wild men, the wildlings of Game of Thrones; the old tapestries show the wild men attacking the castle. It was a big mistake: it helped for a while, then they overthrew us. Game of Thrones is based on our history, with Edomites put everywhere in place of our people, who were fighting against Esau.

“But we will return and build the desolate places.” During the Renaissance they came and started to rebuild; that is when they started to conquer us. They built up Europe and they built up America. “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”: I, God Almighty.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” That is what Paul is talking about. The border, the beginning and the ending of wickedness, is Edom. “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: God has righteous anger against them forever. When people say that is just our interpretation, their own Bible dictionary says Edom is the scene of great future judgment, and white people put that dictionary together.

Another precept to start using. “Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial.” Read verse 4: “thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon.” The king of Babylon is Babylon the great: Esau, Edom. Edom shall not be joined with the other nations in burial.

“Because thou hast destroyed thy land”: they allowed 9/11 to happen, they allowed COVID to happen. “And slain thy people”: they are the ones that slay their own people.

“The seed of evildoers shall never be renowned.” Renowned means celebrated, famous, widely recognised for a skill, achievement or quality: not just widely known but highly respected and esteemed. What race on earth is celebrated? It is not China. The white man is the one that is famous, recognised for technology, the most highly respected on the earth, held in such high esteem especially among black women. They are not going to be respected anymore.

“The burden of Babylon.” People think the wicked will be revealed on his own. No: “Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”, and the banner is the Bible. “Exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand”: reprove them, correct them. “That they may go into the gates of the nobles”: the nobles are not black people. The nobles are white folks.

“I have commanded my sanctified ones”: that is us. “I have also called my mighty ones for mine anger”: the mighty ones are the angels.

So the wicked is revealed by God's people lifting up the Bible and going into the gates of the nobles with it.

The spirit of the Lord's mouth is his word, and his word is where the power is. “Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.” When we speak God's word, it is fire, and the people that hear it are the wood.

When Christ speaks, it is like fire. “And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: the ICBM missiles, all that technology, their satellites across the globe. “Which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest”: a tempest of fire.

“And shall lay before them their evil thoughts”: Christ is going to open up their minds and lay their sin before them. “And the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame: and he shall destroy them without labour by the law.”

God is saying his law is fire. In this physical realm we read the Bible and do not see the spiritual effect it has, because our eyes are closed. So speak the word; that is all you have to do. Don't use clever words; use the word of God, whether they hear or forbear. Even those that reject it go home tossing and turning in their bed, and go to Sunday school seeing it is not what the pastor said. The way we break it down haunts them.

God had to remind us again after Jeremiah 5: “Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” We have to believe that. Sometimes we only believe what we can see, but the angels are all around us; we just don't see them. The word consumes the wicked as the spirit of his mouth.

“Whose coming is after the working of Satan” goes back to Genesis 4. The Lord speaks to Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” Cain, if you obey me, won't I accept you? “And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door”: if you break my commandments, sin lies at your door.

“And unto thee shall be his desire”: now he switches and speaks to Satan. Unto Satan shall be Cain's desire, “and thou shalt rule over him.” Satan rules over Cain. His coming is after the working of Satan.

Christ said this to the Pharisees, Israelites who were in love with Rome. “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do”: the desires of your father you will do.

“He was a murderer from the beginning”: that is Cain, not a spiritual demon. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.” Cain is a liar and the father of lies, because Satan is his father. That is the one whose coming is after the working of Satan, with lying wonders.

This is the precept for “even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan”, and it goes together with Genesis 4:7. “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” The wicked man has Satan at his right hand. He follows everything Satan says.

For “all power and signs and lying wonders”: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.”

The signs and wonders go with their science and their technology. Something major is going to happen. We don't know when, but before this kingdom goes down there is going to be a worldwide event to deceive the world, and some, God forbid, will be deceived.

Those signs and miracles let you know it is technology. “And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men”: that is thermonuclear fire.

“And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles.” See what it calls them: miracles. That is the signs and wonders; it says the same thing as Matthew 24 with a different word. “Which he had power to do in the sight of the beast”: of Europe, the Europeans.
“The love of the truth”: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That is the love they don't want.

“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” They did not want that; they rejected it. To receive the love of the truth is to keep his commandments.

“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” So the love of God and the truth go back to his laws: of course, his laws in Christ. You cannot ignore Christ. Those who “received not the love of the truth” rejected the law.

What do they love about this world instead? “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Our people don't want to be content with the love of the Lord; they want to go above and beyond, so they want to be rich. All these contracts for entertainers have a catch, a gotcha moment.

“For the love of money is the root of all evil.” So when you are asked to work seven days a week or on the Sabbath, don't call and ask whether it is okay to break the Sabbath. We are not going to tell you to break God's laws; that is between you and the Lord. “Which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

Esau talks about us and bids on us: who goes into which sport. That is in Get Out, and it is what the man said in the clip: we have our meetings and you are not invited. And in Trick Baby they say it plainly: the smart ones are moved up into white society to neutralize them; he loses his identity, becomes alien to his brothers, and in his love for the creature comforts, except for his colour, becomes one of them. Brandon Tatum fits that 100%.

They raise him up and make him, politically; then, as at the beginning of the class, they get rid of all those black leaders in the government. “For such as in their life have received benefits”: the riches, the fame, the fortune. “And have not known me”: have not known the one true God.

“And they that have loathed my law”: they hated God's laws. That is the same thing as Thessalonians: “because they received not the love of the truth.” “While they had yet liberty”: while the brothers were on the street preaching and teaching. “And, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.”

And the judgment: “The same must know it after death by pain.”

“I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears upon them.” God said, I will choose your delusion. That is the strong delusion of 2 Thessalonians 2:11 sent on those who reject his laws, and that is why no scripture you pull will bring them out of it.

Hold the traditions: “Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” In our gathering together among ourselves, the law says to be kindly affectioned one toward another, with brotherly love, preferring one another.

It offends white folks that we gather and read scriptures among ourselves; the other nations hate that. A sister told how she paid for some little black children's snacks when their cards were declined at the register, and the white cashier was angry about it while every white person walked right past them. They hate to see us stick together, and when we look out for each other, we become dangerous.

“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired. Nobody wants to be with us; no nation wants to take us in. That is why Romans 12:10 commands us to be kindly affectioned one to another: the nation nobody desires has to gather together and prefer one another.

sense.text:
“Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Paul is addressing Esau. He is telling the Israelites in Rome: remember Esau.

Why not just say Rome? Letters were read at Rome's checkpoints, and you could not speak any ill against Rome. So they said, we won't say Rome, we'll say Esau. That is who it is talking about. And Paul is speaking on God's behalf: that is what God says.

Their own scholars wrote it: an 1890 Bible dictionary records that from Edom came the kings who reigned in Italy and built up Rome to be great among the nations, that Italy, Greece and all the western provinces became filled with Idumeans, which is the Greek and Roman name for Edom, and that the prophets call the whole of that nation by the name of Edom; that Julius Caesar was an Idumean and that the Jews believed Titus was an Edomite. Not Japheth. Edom.
“Is there unrighteousness with God?” Is God unrighteous? “God forbid.” The answer is no.
“I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.” Go back to verse 13: the mercy is going to Jacob.

“So then it is not of him that willeth.” You cannot will yourself to be the people of God, the merciful vessel God will have mercy on. It has nothing to do with positive thinking; you cannot positively change the mind of God.

“Nor of him that runneth.” You cannot run throughout the earth building churches and make yourself the people of God. “But of God that sheweth mercy.”

“For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh.” Now he is comparing Esau to Pharaoh. Pharaoh was the world's superpower. In the time of Paul and the apostles the Pharaoh of the time was Rome; at that time Esau was Rome, the world's superpower.

“That my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” When God brought Egypt down, all the nations said, we heard what your God did for you. Rome was not smitten; Rome just transformed, and now we are here in America. The Lord is going to smite this place, and what happened in the time of Moses will happen in this time when this country is destroyed: we heard what your God did for you.

“Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up.” God made Pharaoh the world's superpower, and America right now is the world's superpower: more bombs and greater technology than any nation, bases all over the planet, able to fight on different fronts at the same time. No other nation has that. That is why everybody fears America. Nobody can defeat them one on one; God said, I have to take them down.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy”: that is Jacob. “And whom he will he hardeneth”: he hardened Pharaoh, and he is going to harden Esau.

So no, the white man is not going to let millions of Israelites take his planes and boats to the wilderness. That is not in the Bible. Some were told to sell everything and go to one land to be delivered and had their passports taken. When the Palestinians were told to go to Egypt, Egypt blocked them. Nobody reads the Bible anymore. They have to go down.
“Why doth he yet find fault?” If he makes one vessel to honour and one to dishonour, why does God find fault? “For who hath resisted his will?” Nobody.

“Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God?” Who in the hell are you to reply against God?

“Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” Think of a writer making a movie: you need a good guy, a bad guy, a supporting cast. Why do I have to be the bad guy? Because I am paying you to be the bad guy. Paul uses the same reasoning. The white man read the Bible, saw the script and said, that's not me, I am not Esau; we're going to change the script. And people listen to him.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay?” The pot cannot say to the one making it, why are you making me like this? It stays quiet, and its maker forms it and shapes it whichever way he does.

“Of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour”: that is Jacob. “And another unto dishonour”: that is Esau.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath”, his anger, “and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” The vessels are the people: the people of wrath, fitted, which means created, to destruction. Created to be destroyed. Another word for destruction there is perdition.

“Endured with much longsuffering” is what Psalm 50 means: these things hast thou done, and I kept silence.

precepts.why:
“That my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” “For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments.” This is ancient Egypt, but bring it up to today: the enchantments today are called science, Esau's science, his technology.

“Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” As it was then, it is going to be now. Today they say, you're not the Israelites, you're just a Gentile. When the destruction comes, the great death, that is when they will acknowledge that we are the sons of God.

“And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth: In much knowledge the Lord hath divided them, and made their ways diverse.” He divided men and made their ways diverse.

“Some of them hath he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself: but some of them hath he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places.” Some he cursed: that is Esau.

“As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him.” That is the potter of Romans 9:21, with one vessel unto honour, Jacob, and another unto dishonour, Esau.

“Endured with much longsuffering”: verse 21 is the point, but start at 16, where we always start. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” The wicked took up the old covenant as Jews and the new covenant as Christians. “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” And notice: the ones doing all the killing are Christians. Never forget that.

“When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him.” America did not say anything when it saw Amalek taking the land of Palestine; it saw the genocide and said, we'll help you. When they took over Australia and South Africa, America sat back and allowed it. A black congressman does anything corrupt and he is called out and fired; they do it and nobody sees anything. Just like with these murders: nobody knows anything, and the coroner in the Nolan Wells case will not release his report. “And hast been partaker with adulterers”: sexual abuse and rape. Look at the Epstein case.

“Thou givest thy mouth to evil”: they say they are Christians and kill you in the same breath. “And thy tongue frameth deceit”: Jesus is white and was born December 25th. “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother”: their Christian theology makes Jacob the evil son and Esau the righteous one, just as they would make Cain good and Abel bad. “Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”: they slander us day by day as the worst criminals on earth, black-on-black crime. In 2016 alone America dropped 26,171 bombs on seven countries; Trump has bombed more countries than any modern president; around 50,000 children have been killed in Palestine in less than a year. Put all the killings by black people in this country together for 30 years and you do not have that. Know these statistics, or they will make you the bad guy.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” That is what “endured with much longsuffering” means. Some say, I don't believe in God: why didn't he save us in slavery, in Jim Crow? He said, I saw all these things and I kept silent. I'm waiting. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: God isn't judging us, so surely he is a white man. “But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”: he sets the Israelites, the children of Jacob, in order before them, and that is what the world sees right now.

God raised up the superpower so that nobody can defeat them one on one; he has to take them down himself. “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered”: your sins. “Yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

You are not putting him on a cross anymore. He said, I am not going to meet you as a man; I am going to meet you as God Almighty.

In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on God's behalf: Jacob have I loved, Esau have I hated. That is what God says. But God's law to us is “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”: a wicked brother. “Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.”

Brothers, use this verse to your advantage. Don't run from it.

Why does God say don't abhor him? A brother once said he could not join because he was on medication: he could not work, because when he sat in the office or did construction he looked at white people and wanted to harm them.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you cannot walk around saying I hate your guts. You think you are going to keep a job? You are going to lose everything.

People ask whether this teaching makes people angry. Yes, they get angry, and the Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not.” The sin would be to start murdering people or stealing.

There were brothers who got strong learning to fight, and it came out on the news that they were doing home invasions and burglaries, beating Edomites. Professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. Some camps teach that, and their leaders have no jobs: they live off the congregation or work where they never deal with a boss, so they can speak that way without repercussions and get mad at brothers who don't. Don't fall into that.

As the character said in American Gods: anger gets stuff done. Oppression makes a wise man mad, but not mad to go kill everybody: let's organize, let's do better.

“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” If it be possible. There have been times on the news where it was impossible, where you had to fight, because some people are irate and unreasonable. In A Time to Kill, when they raped and beat Samuel Jackson's daughter, he was not letting that go, and every father understands that. There are certain things that make you snap.

About being angry: “But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment.” The key is “without a cause.” If I am mad with you and have no reason to be, I am in danger of judgment. But when somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one, you have a cause.

Shut up, you little pansy boys out there: to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you are not capable of violence, you are just harmless, a useless man. Be angry, and sin not.

sense.text:
Read because, when we go into the gates of the nobles, there is always a consequence for revealing the devil. The white man has done so much evil, taught so many lies, and is hiding in this earth as the righteous, as Jews and Christians. Now here we come revealing him, and he will not just sit there.

“After ye were illuminated”: once you got the understanding of who you are and who Christ is, “ye endured a great fight of afflictions.” This was in Paul's time.

“Whilst ye were made a gazingstock”: when you are on the street teaching, you are a gazingstock: why are they always on the corner, why do they always have that Bible? That time is related to us today. “Whilst ye became companions of them that were so used”: you became friends and brethren of those used like you are being used.

“For ye had compassion of me in my bonds”: when I was in prison. “And took joyfully the spoiling of your goods”: the robbing of your homes and houses. There was a penalty for speaking against Rome; their homes were robbed and taken. We read right by it without looking into it. It didn't faze them: we are going to get it all back a hundredfold.

“Knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.” That heaven is not pie in the sky; it is going to be on earth. That is the Lord's prayer: thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven.

“Cast not away therefore your confidence.” They had their homes, their money, their livelihood taken. Especially for the women: I don't have a house anymore, my property is gone, my garden is gone. And the husband has to say, babe, we are going to get all this back and more. Losing it would mess with your faith. It “hath great recompence of reward.”
“For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.” That is what we want: after we have done the will of God, to receive the promise.
“For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.” Paul was encouraging them, and that is how we have to encourage one another.

“Now the just shall live by faith”: we must live by our faith in Christ. “But if any man draw back”: if any one of you, man or woman, draws back from this truth to do your own thing, I'll be a Muslim, I'll go back to the Christian church, “my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” God will not have pleasure in you.

“But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition”: we have to be resolved in mind and spirit. Why does it say draw back unto perdition? Because when you draw back you are joining the white man, who goes into perdition. “But of them that believe to the saving of the soul.”

precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”: the mobs, the military. “And they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” That is Christianity, the religion of this country: leading you right back to the Christian church.

“And they that consent unto them”, who agree with them because they have battle fatigue, tired of reproving their people and wanting to live a whole life all over again, “shall be had in derision and in reproach”, mocked, “and trodden under foot”, ultimately put to death. That is drawing back unto perdition.

“For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Just as it was back then, it is going to happen again; prepare yourselves. “They shall be like mad men, sparing none”: if they catch you, they will not spare you. But Christ said if they persecute you in one city, flee to another, so some cities and states will be relatively calm, and we have to identify where we can go.

“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” That is what happened in Hebrews 10:34. “Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

Read with Hebrews 10:34, the spoiling of their goods. Start above, at verse 27: “Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ.” A Christian reads that as love, love, love. No. The good news of Christ is that he died for the 12 tribes, and is coming back to deliver the Israelites, destroy the nations, set up the kingdom on this planet and have the Israelites rule. Guess what that is called? Treason. When they nailed Christ to the cross they called him King of the Jews: treason. He was talking about another kingdom, and they couldn't get him on anything else. We say the same thing he said, and today there are laws on the books where speaking against Christianity or America falls under extremism.

“That ye stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel”: not doing separate things, a Mexican camp here, a Puerto Rican camp there.

“And in nothing terrified by your adversaries”: you have enemies who despise the gospel, who will speak against us and come against us. “Which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.” They took homes, they took houses, they put people to death, as they did to James. To them it is an evident sign of hell, of destruction; to us it is a sign of salvation: my home was taken, I was incarcerated, put to death, and that is a sign of salvation.

“For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake.” It is not enough just to believe; everybody says they believe, but how many are willing to suffer for his sake? “Having the same conflict which ye saw in me”: what Christ went through, Paul went through, and so will we.

“But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them”: no torment of the lake of fire.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery.” This is the same thing as Philippians 1:28. They call you an activist with nothing better to do, always complaining; but Christ was an activist, always out preaching repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand, and so were the 12 apostles. They say you had a miserable life: you could have had the good job, worked on the Sabbath for big money, a mansion, a yacht and a string of polo ponies, and a white woman on your arm; but no, you chose to keep the Sabbath and take the job that pays for five or six days. That is what the unwise see.

“And their going from us to be utter destruction”: that is what the wicked say, that it is perdition. “But they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men”, the same as Philippians 1, “yet is their hope full of immortality.”

“And having been a little chastised”: see what God calls it. For the moment you are in pain, but it is just a little chastisement. “They shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the righteous is like a burnt offering to the Lord.

sense.text:
A new thing Christians are pushing: that other nations will come into the kingdom through the same gate Abraham came through, because Abraham was not an Israelite. Abraham was not one of the 12, but he was the father of the 12.

So read what Christ said about Abraham: “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.” Find out who is coming from the east and the west. Zechariah answers it: God's people, Zion, the Israelites. That cuts his argument about Abraham. And the very fact that he has to address it shows the teaching is impacting the church.

precepts.why:
Who is coming from the east and west? “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

That is only the Israelites. The ones coming from the east and west to sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are God's people.

Read verse 1 with it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I was jealous for Zion.” For who? For Zion. Zion is not all nations on the planet. The ones coming from the east country and the west country to sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Zion.

They always go to Abraham as though that brings in the other nations, and Paul had to clean up that confusion back then: “Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.”

Abraham had other children who had nothing to do with the 12 tribes of Israel. The calling is on Isaac: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the 12 tribes. That is a wrap: close your Bible up and sit down.

sense.text:
“There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.” A scoffer mocks, ridicules and treats others with contempt, dismissing beliefs he disagrees with as silly or stupid; not just disagreeing but expressing insolent doubt and derision. In religious use it is one who openly opposes God and divine truth: arrogant, closed-minded and fuelled by pride.

Among the reasons people scoff at the Bible is the problem of evil and suffering: why would a good and all-powerful God permit harm? A man who preached for 15 years now says it is all a lie, that black people are not Israelites, and that if the God of the Bible were real he would hate him: slavery, Jim Crow, the Trail of Tears, and Jesus did nothing. That is trauma. He has a child with stage four brain cancer. When bad things happen, people turn around and blame God, and that is why many become atheists. But when bad things happen to us we have to do what Job did: praise the Lord. He did not charge God foolishly, and we cannot charge God foolishly, knowing he has his reasons.

“And saying, Where is the promise of his coming?” Where is Yeshua, where is Jesus, or whoever you say he is? “For since the fathers fell asleep”, since they died, “all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation”: everything is the same as from creation.

“For this they willingly are ignorant of.” The Bible says they are willingly ignorant. “The earth standing out of the water and in the water”, “being overflowed with water, perished”: the flood in the time of Noah. They had the same scoffers in the time of Noah, and God put all of them to death.

“But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire.” Notice that heavens has an s: it is not talking about the sky. It is talking about the ruling kingdoms on the earth.

“Against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” God is going to get rid of these ungodly men, and it says perdition of the ungodly because they follow that man of sin, the son of perdition.

“That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” He did not change the subject. Go back to verse 4: since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as from the beginning of the creation. That is thousands of years. So Peter reminds us about time.

“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”: they say God is being slack. “But is longsuffering”, as read in Romans 9, “to us-ward”: to us Israelites. “Not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance”: that all is talking about the Israelites.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”: unexpected. “The heavens shall pass away with a great noise”: boom. “The earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up”: the works, the things done on this planet. That includes your twerking, your dressing out of order, all of it. He is going to get rid of all of it.

“What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness.” We have to change the way we speak. Once the inner man is changed, it changes our speech, the way we dress, and the way we conduct ourselves.
